title: When the Atlas Burns
premise: In 1847, Coral Halloran, a mapmaker's apprentice in a famine-stricken port town, has spent fifteen years perfecting the art of being overlooked while secretly completing the atlas his hanged master died for. When a census taker's probing questions expose the forged identities keeping his family fed, Coral must smuggle them onto an emigrant ship with only two berths for three people. He gives the berth to his sister, stays behind to burn the atlas pages that could hang them all, and discovers that justice comes not from escaping but from leaving the truth behind for those who return.
about_author: Bram Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing emigration records from the Great Famine era. They write historical fiction about the ordinary people history forgot to name.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Coral Halloran, POV. While finishing the master's final atlas plate by candlelight, Coral answers a census taker's routine questions until one lands wrong: how many children were born in this house? His careful lie cracks, and he realizes the taker already knows the answer. The emotional beat is dread blooming into certainty: invisibility was always borrowed time, and the debt has come due.

chapters.title: Two Berths, Three Names
chapters.summary: Coral's sister Nell, POV. Nell discovers Coral has been forging passage papers and confronts him at the harbor office where only two berths remain on the last ship before the port closes. Their brother Taddeus is feverish and cannot walk far; their mother refuses to leave the grave of the hanged mapmaker. The beat is love sharpened into an impossible arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: What the Atlas Knows
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. The census taker returns with soldiers, hunting the forged documents and the seditious maps that chart hidden escape routes along the coast. Coral races to finish the atlas's final plate, then chooses which pages to save and which to feed to the fire, understanding that burning knowledge is both betrayal and protection. Climax: he trades himself for his family's departure, naming himself as the forger.

chapters.title: The Coastline Remains
chapters.summary: Nell, POV, years later in America. Nell opens a parcel smuggled out after Coral's trial: the saved atlas plates and a letter explaining he survived transportation, not the gallows, because the burned pages left nothing to prove. She begins redrawing the coastlines for other fugitives. The resolution lands on justice outside the law: survival as inheritance, and maps as the quietest form of rebellion.
